🔥🇲🇽 18.5 MILLION MEDICINES LEFT TO EXPIRE AT MEXICO'S CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL

The FGR and the Health Ministry's internal control unit are investigating how 18.5 million medications were allowed to expire at the Hospital Infantil between 2020 and 2024 — including 390,000 doses of oncology drugs like methotrexate and vincristine meant for children with cancer — a 121.4-million-peso hit to the treasury. Hospital staff filed 211 complaints in just three days of inspections.

🇲🇽🌳 MEXICO SLAMS THE DOOR ON MINING IN ALL 232 PROTECTED AREAS

Effective today, Semarnat bars every mining concession holder from exploring or extracting inside Mexico's 232 federal protected natural areas without prior environmental-impact authorization — retroactively, even for concessions granted before May 2023. Conanp will now issue a binding technical report on each request. Concessions the neoliberal era waved through now have to answer to the land.

🇲🇽🛢️ OIL HITS $80.80 — BUT WASHINGTON'S WAR PREMIUM NEVER REACHES THE PUMP

Global crude jumped to $80.80 a barrel this week — Mexico's mix closed at $80.88, above the $77.30 Hacienda budgeted. But the windfall skips Pemex: the state fuel subsidy holds gasoline at 24 pesos and diesel at 27 per liter, absorbing the spike so a war premium in the Gulf never reaches Mexican drivers. Per La Jornada, that cap is exactly what keeps domestic inflation contained.

🇲🇽📊 MEXICO'S ECONOMY SHIFTED INTO SECOND GEAR

The "Mexico is collapsing" narrative met the data again. Per El Financiero, the economy went from 0.4% growth in Q1 to 1.8% in Q2 — more than four times faster. Services, two-thirds of GDP, grew 2.2% annually in June; industry crawled back into positive territory. All of it under Trump's tariff siege and a peso the doomers keep trying to bury. Acceleration, not collapse.

🇲🇽🧠 MEXICO CITY MOVES TO MAKE EMOTIONAL WELLBEING A CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT

Clara Brugada is sending the CDMX Congress a reform to recognize emotional wellbeing as a fundamental right — free psychological care in every school, a new citywide mental-health system. It builds on "Vida Plena, Corazón Contento," which reached over 1 million people this school year and whose specialists identified and helped 147 suicide-risk cases. "Arriving on time can save lives," Brugada said. Two of every three CDMX teens report emotional distress; the 4T is treating it as a right, not a private expense.

🚨🇲🇽 SHEINBAUM: "UNHEARD OF" FOR A MEXICAN TO SIC ICE ON HIS OWN

A Mexican man watched migrants welcome President Sheinbaum in New York and posted "ICE, do your thing" — cheering the deportation machine on against his own countrymen. Salinas Pliego amplified it. Sheinbaum's answer: "It's unheard of that a Mexican would post this, speaking against Mexicans in the United States." The comprador instinct, said out loud.

🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO REFUSES RUBIO'S SUMMIT AGAINST "THE LEFT"

Marco Rubio convened a summit against "left-wing political terrorism." Mexico said no. President Sheinbaum invoked Article 89 of the Constitution — self-determination, non-intervention — and drew the line: "Political matters shouldn't be turned into a security issue unless there's an actual crime to prosecute." Washington wants to criminalize an ideology; Mexico won't lend its name to it.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 ZAPATISTAS SAIL SOLAR PANELS AND MEDICINE TO BLOCKADED CUBA

The EZLN just ran the blockade. Capitán Marcos confirmed the Zapatista boat Lacandona reached Cuba alongside Open Arms' vessel Astral, delivering solar panels, photovoltaic equipment and medicine to Havana's Juan Manuel Márquez children's hospital. Mexican rebels crossing the Gulf to keep the lights on in a hospital the US embargo is trying to darken — announced from Chiapas at a gathering they named "War Against Humanity."

🔥🇲🇽 BRITISH COURT CALLS SALINAS PLIEGO'S SPYING "AN AFFRONT TO JUSTICE"

Mexico's loudest 4T opponent, billionaire Ricardo Salinas Pliego, just lost in a UK court — which ruled he committed "an abuse of process" by hiring spy firm Black Cube to secretly record a rival's lawyer over dinner. The judges called the recording "an affront to justice" and "a form of corruption," and unfroze the assets he'd tried to seize. The oligarch who still won't pay his back taxes to Mexico runs the same playbook abroad.

🇲🇽💵 THE PESO CLOSES NEAR 17.40 — DOLLAR DOWN 7.6% AGAINST IT IN A YEAR

The peso closed around 17.40 to the dollar on Tuesday, with the greenback down 7.6% year-over-year against it and exchange volatility (7.07%) sitting below its reference — what El Financiero calls the peso's "resilience." Nearshoring inflows and 2026 World Cup spending keep feeding the currency, even as Washington keeps threatening Mexico with tariffs.
